Conclusions
In summary, an efficient catalytic room temperature aerobic
oxidation has been developed. With 5 mol% of
\mathsf { F e } ( \mathsf { N O } _ { 3 } ) _ { 3 } { \cdot } \mathsf { 9 H } _ { 2 } \mathsf { O }
as
the single catalyst and 1 atm of pure
or oxygen in air as the
oxidant, different types of aldehydes with various useful function-
al groups could be oxidized to acid smoothly. The reaction could
be conducted easily on 50 mmol scale with
\mathsf { O } _ { 2 }
or a slow air flow.
Based on careful mechanistic study, it is believed that the reaction
proceeds via two plausible pathways. Further studies including
mechanism details are being conducted actively in this laboratory.

Conclusions
In summary, an efficient catalytic room temperature aerobic
oxidation has been developed. With 5 mol% of
\mathsf { F e } ( \mathsf { N O } _ { 3 } ) _ { 3 } { \cdot } \mathsf { 9 H } _ { 2 } \mathsf { O }
as
the single catalyst and 1 atm of pure
or oxygen in air as the
oxidant, different types of aldehydes with various useful function-
al groups could be oxidized to acid smoothly. The reaction could
be conducted easily on 50 mmol scale with
\mathsf { O } _ { 2 }
or a slow air flow.
Based on careful mechanistic study, it is believed that the reaction
proceeds via two plausible pathways. Further studies including
mechanism details are being conducted actively in this laboratory.
